popover.$comment: A popover is a piece of the page that has been lifted off it for a moment, not an annotation laid over it — so its surface is `pct.surface` and its text `pct.text`, exactly what a card in the page is made of. That is the whole difference from the tooltip, whose inverted surface says "read me and forget me": the content here is something the user works IN, and a panel that inverted the page's own colours would ask them to work in a strip of night.
popover.$comment-panel-border: The edge is `border-strong` rather than `border`, and for the dialog's reason one floor down: the panel stands on the page rather than over a veil, so the only thing separating a light panel from a light page is this line. A shadow is not that thing — it goes with the mode that takes shadows away.
popover.$comment-panel-max-width: Narrower than the dialog's 480px and wider than the tooltip's 280px, and the number says what the component is for: a popover hangs off a control, so a panel as wide as a dialog would cover the thing it belongs to on any screen a phone has.

panel-gap.$description: Gap between the panel's heading and its content.

popover.$comment-heading-font-size: One step below the dialog's heading (`md` against `lg`), because the two headings answer different questions: a modal's title is the only thing on the screen that matters, a popover's is a label on a panel the page around it is still holding up.
